summary: The term "Programmer Art" refers to an aesthetic and visual style that originates from software and video game development, particularly in indie games, early shareware and personal projects from programmers.
description:
The term "Programmer Art" refers to an aesthetic and visual style that originates from software and video game development, particularly in indie games, early shareware and personal projects from programmers.

Although any art made by a programmer could be classified as "programmer art" , the term refers specifically to the characteristic unpolished style said to be the result of the lack of artistic skills among "logical-minded" coders [ 1 ] [ 2 ] . It often consists of placeholder elements "thrown together", with the intent to be replaced with a more consistent artstyle later. This manifests with characters and objects made of primitive shapes with high-contrast colors, a disregard of style cohesion and of consistent anatomy or perspective in favor of more abstract styles and an extensive use of default system fonts, palettes and sound effects. In pixel art, the criticized "pillow" shading style is sometimes used [ 3 ] when sprites are not simply flat-colored. Historically, when computers were more limited in their capabilities, monochrome alphanumeric symbols were commonly used to denote the elements of the video-game.

As the indie game scene grew, fondness for what are seen as more primitive styles started to appear across unprofessional shareware of the early internet, and the style started to be intentionally simulated by artists.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Functionalism, representativeness, time-efficiency, amateur creativity
